subject: fuaran-dotnet
$comment: What the proof leg COSTS, declared per module, so that a growth in prover time is named rather than discovered when CI times out. `proofs/check.ps1` (through `proofs/kit/check-proof-leg.ps1`) reads this file: every green CHECK line prints the module's measured seconds beside its budget, and a run over budget prints a named COST warning — never a failure on its own, because prover time varies by machine and by load and a budget is a smoke detector rather than a gate. `check.ps1 -Strict` promotes the warnings to a red leg for a session that wants one. This is NOT `proofs.json`: that file is the claims ladder — what is proved, tested and assumed, at a closed set of levels — and a wall-clock budget is a claim at none of those levels and is not per-claim but per-module. Coverage is checked BOTH ways: a module the leg checks with no entry here, and an entry here for a module the leg does not check, are each a COST warning naming what to do. Hand-authored; the seeding rule below says how a number is arrived at, and bumping one is a recorded act. Each entry also carries a `floorSeconds`, and that number is a GATE rather than a smoke detector: a module that verifies in less than its floor fails the leg on the spot, because a run faster than the module can possibly be is not evidence of speed but of a cache that was not cold. The two rules sit in `seeding` and `floorSeeding` below, and the asymmetry between warning above and failing below is argued in the second of them.

seeding.rule: budgetSeconds = max(2 x the slowest observed cold-cache run, minimumBudgetSeconds), rounded up to the next 10s.
seeding.$comment: The tolerance is applied ONCE, here, when a number is seeded — `check.ps1` multiplies nothing, so the pair it prints is the measurement against the ceiling and there is no second arithmetic to hold in your head. Seed from the SLOWEST observed cold run rather than the median: concurrent sessions on one machine can inflate a cold check by ~1.8x with nothing about the tree changed, so a budget seeded from the median fires on a busy afternoon and teaches a reader to ignore it. `minimumBudgetSeconds` is the floor UNDER THE CEILING, for the sub-5s modules where 2x is inside ordinary process-start noise; it is a different thing from an entry's `floorSeconds`, which is the per-module time floor below, and the two are named apart deliberately.

cachedRead.rule: thresholdSeconds = about twice the slowest CACHED read measured on the pinned prover; appliesFromFastestSeconds = three times the threshold. A module whose recorded fastestSeconds is at or above appliesFromFastestSeconds and whose cold check finishes under thresholdSeconds FAILS the leg as a probable cached read; a module below it rests on the cache provenance check alone.
cachedRead.$comment: Carried from the proof kit's own declaration (fuaran-core#399), measured on the same pinned prover the kit asset pins: a cached read lands at 0.18s to 0.51s whatever the module costs cold, so one absolute threshold serves every module. Replaces the per-module floors, which the kit's engine retired (it refuses a floorSeeding block or a floorSeconds entry). Re-measure on this repository's own runs as they accumulate; a re-seed is recorded.

modules.note: The kit's shared twin record, opened read-only from the pinned kit asset because WireDecode opens it (since the kit's 0.40.0). No model's subject, so it carries no ladder row. Numbers carried from the kit's own entry (fuaran-core#504): it checks in about a second, so the minimum budget applies.

The decode combinators over the `jval` value model, COPIED from the kit's repository and declared in ../copies.json — generic in its numeric carriers, so nothing here re-states the kit's own theorem. Default context, no scoped options; the cost is ordinary and most of the spread between machines is the machine. SEEDED HERE rather than inherited: the kit's own entry is a measurement on a different machine under a different load, and a budget seeded from somebody else's clock is not a measurement. Cold quaked run on this dev machine under the leg's own flags, `check.ps1 -Runs 1 -SkipOracleHost`, with an idle tree: 17s. Budget 40s by the seeding rule (2 x 17 rounded up to the next 10s); floor 8s by floorSeeding (17 halved, rounded down). ONE observation, so the floor is the conservative end of a single sample — re-seed it DOWNWARDS as a recorded act the first time a genuinely faster cold run is seen, per floorSeeding, rather than leaving a gate that fires on a faster runner.

The GENERATED model of THIS repository's wire vocabulary, emitted by `Fuaran.Core.Idl.Codegen`'s F* target from `src/Fuaran.UI.Idl/idl.json`. Carries `#set-options "--ext context_pruning"` INSIDE the generated file, because it opens the whole decode model and declares dozens of types; if this budget is ever bumped, check the option is still in force before reading the growth as ordinary. Twenty of forty-three kinds are modelled — the selection is `FStarTarget.proofKinds` and the emitted header names each of the other twenty-three with its reason (see README.md 'Coverage' for the measurement that chose it). CHECKED but not EXTRACTED (`$proofOnly` in check.ps1). WHAT A BUMP MEANS HERE: its size is a function of the vocabulary it is generated from, so growth means the VOCABULARY grew — a kind whose types the envelope already carries adds one constructor to three definitions — and the generation diff is what makes any such change deliberate. SEEDED from a cold quaked run on this dev machine under the leg's own flags, idle tree: 94s. Budget 190s by the seeding rule; floor 47s by floorSeeding. ONE observation — see WireDecode's note on re-seeding a floor downwards.

THE LEG'S WHOLE COST, by two orders of magnitude; read this number before reading any other. The generated ROUND TRIP over `Vocabulary` (`dec_node (enc_node x) == Ok x` for every value of every modelled type), plus `dec_node_total`. Emitted by the same target from the same walk as the model, ONE LEMMA PER CONSTRUCTOR and one per PRESENCE PATTERN (fuaran-core#168): a constructor with two or more conditional members is split into `...__p<bits>` lemmas whose `requires` pins every conditional member present or absent, so no query carries more than one constructor's object shapes. 682 lemma heads, 548 of them presence patterns. MEASURED on the pinned prover, cold, with the leg's own flags, one `check.ps1 -Runs 1 -SkipOracleHost` leg on this dev machine: 5040s (1h24m), every query 3/3 under --quake, green. Budget 10100s by the seeding rule. WHERE THE COST IS, which is the fact a future reader needs before reading a bump as ordinary: it is the NODE ENVELOPE, not the kinds. Emitted at a ONE-kind selection this script still carries 318 of those 682 lemma heads, because the envelope's five conditional members are 32 presence patterns over a closure of records and unions that every kind pays for; each further envelope-closed kind adds roughly twenty. So a bump here means the ENVELOPE grew - a new optional `nodeFields` member DOUBLES the pattern family - and a new kind of the sort `FStarTarget.proofKinds` selects is nearly free. See README.md 'Coverage'. THE BINDING RESOURCE IS MEMORY, NOT TIME: at its peak the prover held 90.6 GB committed (7.2 GB resident) on a 31.5 GB machine, so most of that 5040s is paging. A machine with less page file will not merely be slower; it will fail. A second prover started against a 1-kind copy of this script WHILE that was running died with `Fatal error: allocation failure during minor GC` at 11 minutes - recorded as a CONTENTION observation and NOT as a property of the 1-kind script, which has not been checked alone. FLOOR DELIBERATELY 0, and that is an argument rather than an omission. floorSeeding would put it at 2520s from this single sample, but the sample was taken on a machine that also ran two full repository gates and a second prover, so the true fastest cold run is unknown and certainly lower. A 2520s floor would FAIL the leg on a quiet or faster machine - the one direction Phase 164's asymmetry says to fear - and a floor exists to catch a run at or near ZERO seconds, which 0 still does for a cache that was not cold. Re-seed it upwards, as a recorded act, from a fastest run measured on an idle machine.
